title: Workforce
text:
NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Educational attainment strongly correlates with income levels, workforce productivity, and economic growth. It helps gauge the skill level and potential earning capacity of a population.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S1501) • Population 25 and older
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Understanding income disparities by educational attainment and sex provides insights into the effectiveness of educational systems in equipping individuals with skills for higher-paying jobs and highlights potential gender-based income gaps, which can be indicative of gender equality issues.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table B20004) • Population 25 and older with earnings
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Travel time to work is significant as it directly impacts worker productivity and transportation costs. It also informs urban planning and labor market dynamics, influencing economic development and accessibility to jobs.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table B08135) • Travel time one way
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Understanding how people commute to work helps assess the efficiency of transportation infrastructure, which can impact productivity and business operations. It also influences urban planning and investment decisions, as well as energy consumption and environmental considerations. Additionally, tracking transportation methods can reveal trends in workforce mobility and inform policies that affect job accessibility and economic opportunities.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table B08128)
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Understanding the age of the housing stock reveals the state of infrastructure and housing quality. Older housing may require more maintenance and renovations, which can drive construction and home improvement industries, thereby boosting economic activity. Additionally, it can inform urban development and land use policies, impacting property values and real estate investments. Lastly, the age of the housing stock can provide insights into population trends, migration patterns, and housing affordability, all of which have significant economic implications.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S2504)
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Knowledge of people’s internet access is an important economic indicator because it reflects digital connectivity, which is increasingly vital for economic participation. It influences business competitiveness and innovation, as companies depend on digital platforms for operations and sales. Internet access also affects workforce capabilities, as remote work and online education become more prevalent. Finally, understanding how people access the internet plays a role in bridging economic disparities, as access can be a factor in determining opportunities and socioeconomic outcomes.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S2801) • Totals may not sum to 100% due to rounding.
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The number of building permits issued can be crucial for gauging the vitality of the construction sector, offering insights into real estate investment trends and potential economic growth. Fluctuations in permit numbers can signal changes in job creation within construction and related industries, serving as a barometer for broader economic activity. A decline in permits may indicate economic challenges, affecting employment and the overall economic environment.
Source: Residential Building Permits Survey County ASC II Files.
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Knowing the median income needed to afford rent and housing costs is essential to evaluate how housing affordability impacts on individuals and the overall economy. This knowledge informs policymakers on ways to address potential disparities, guiding strategies to enhance housing accessibility and promote sustainable economic development.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table Table DP04) • Totals may not sum to 100% due to rounding.
Download Data

title: Regional Datahub
text:
The Upjohn Regional team provides up-to-date measures of labor markets in Southwest Michigan and beyond. These metrics are key to small businesses, nonprofits, larger companies looking to relocate or expand, local and state policymakers, public involvement advocates and civic organizations. To make these metrics more accessible and compelling, our team has developed the Upjohn Regional Data Hub. The Upjohn Regional Data Hub consists of four sections that focus on different economic development indicators: State of the Region, Workforce Indicators, Business Indicators, and Equity Indicators. The data are on the county level and users can select any county in Michigan from the drop-down lists; Southwest Michigan counties are listed first. The Upjohn Regional team will continue to add additional sections of the Data Hub that build on the current concepts.
Please contact us if you have any questions.

title: Business Indicators
text:
NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Real personal consumption expenditures and disposable income are crucial for understanding consumer spending patterns, which drive much of economic activity. These indicators reveal household financial health and confidence, guiding policymakers in assessing fiscal policies and fostering economic growth and stability. “Chained 2017 dollars” is a method of adjusting economic statistics for inflation; values from other years are adjusted to reflect purchasing power of the dollar in 2017. Consumer goods can be classified as durable, nondurable, or services. Durable goods are classified as items that have long periods between successive purchases (ex. cars or home appliances). Nondurable goods are classified as items that have long periods between successive purchases (ex. food or clothing). Services are acts which are paid for (ex. work done by barbers, doctors, mechanics, etc.)
Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (series DSPIC96, PCEDGC96, PCENDC96, and PCESC96)
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Vehicle sales and fuel prices are important economic indicators because they reflect consumer spending and economic confidence, with high sales signaling robust economic activity. Additionally, fuel prices impact transportation costs and disposable income, influencing the economy overall.
Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (series ALTSALES) and U.S. Energy Information Administration (series EMM_EPM0_PTE_NUS_DPG)
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The GDP percent change measures the economy’s growth rate, reflecting overall economic health and stability. It helps policymakers and investors make informed decisions by indicating the pace of economic expansion or contraction.
Source: US BEA (table CAGDP1)
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The percent change in business applications reflects entrepreneurial activity and economic dynamism. A rise in applications suggests increased business formation and economic growth potential, while a decline may indicate reduced economic confidence and future investment.
Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (series BUSAPPWNSAMIYY and BUSAPPWNSAUS)
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Tracking the average annual pay provides insights into income levels and purchasing power within an economy. It helps assess wage trends, labor market conditions, and overall economic well-being, guiding policymaking and business decisions.
Source: BLS QCEW
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Understanding the class of worker in a county is crucial for analyzing labor market dynamics and economic structure. It offers insights into employment patterns, including self-employment, wage and salary jobs, and their contributions to economic activity and workforce composition.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table B08528)

title: Equity
text:
NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Knowing the population with a disability is an important economic indicator because it helps identify potential barriers to workforce participation, highlighting areas where accessible employment opportunities and support services are needed. This information guides policymakers and businesses in making informed decisions about resource allocation and infrastructure improvements. Additionally, understanding the prevalence of disabilities can reveal trends in healthcare demand and social service requirements, impacting overall economic planning.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S1810) • Individual Disability Categories Will Not Sum To Total Population With A Disability
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The unemployment rate for women with children is a key economic indicator as it reflects the challenges they face in balancing work and care giving, which can impact household income and economic stability. It helps policymakers understand the need for supportive measures such as affordable childcare and flexible work arrangements to improve labor force participation. Additionally, this data can inform businesses and governments on how to create family-friendly policies that promote economic growth and gender equality in the workforce.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S2301) • Population 16 and older
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The labor force participation rate for women with children is a key economic indicator, highlighting the challenges they encounter in balancing work and caregiving responsibilities. This rate impacts household income and overall economic stability, providing policymakers with insights into the need for supportive measures like affordable childcare and flexible work options to encourage workforce participation. Additionally, this data can guide businesses and governments in developing family-friendly policies that foster economic growth and promote gender equality in the labor market.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S2301) • Population 16 and older
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The unemployment rate by race is a crucial economic indicator because it highlights disparities in access to job opportunities and economic inclusion across different racial and ethnic groups. It informs policymakers about the need for targeted interventions to address systemic inequalities in education, training, and employment. This data also helps businesses and governments develop equitable hiring practices and policies to promote a more diverse and inclusive workforce, contributing to broader economic stability and social equity.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S2301) • Population 16 and older
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The population below the poverty level, by race, is an important economic indicator as it reveals the extent of economic disparities and social inequities faced by different racial and ethnic groups. It helps policymakers design targeted anti-poverty programs, such as affordable housing, education, and healthcare, to address the unique needs of marginalized communities. This data is also vital for businesses and governments to promote inclusive economic growth, ensuring that all groups have opportunities to improve their living standards and participate fully in the economy.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S1701)
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Health insurance coverage by race is a critical economic indicator because it highlights disparities in access to healthcare, which can affect the overall health and economic well-being of different racial and ethnic groups. This data helps policymakers identify gaps in coverage and design inclusive healthcare policies that ensure equitable access to medical services for all communities. Understanding these disparities allows governments and organizations to address long-term healthcare costs, improve workforce productivity, and promote economic stability by reducing health-related financial burdens.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table S2701) • Population 16 and older
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Vehicles per household is a significant economic indicator as it reflects access to transportation, which directly impacts employment opportunities, access to services, and overall mobility. In regions with limited public transportation, such as many rural and suburban areas in the U.S., households with fewer vehicles may face challenges in commuting to work or school. This data helps policymakers and urban planners address transportation needs, develop infrastructure, and improve transit options, ultimately influencing economic participation and quality of life across different communities.
Source: ACS 2024 5-YR Estimates (table DP04)

NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The employment-to-population ratio is a crucial economic indicator as it reflects the percentage of the working-age population who are employed. It provides insights into labor market health, income levels, productivity, and social stability. Policymakers and investors rely on this ratio to gauge economic well-being and make informed decisions.
Source: BLS LAUS, Upjohn Regional • (p) Preliminary, (e) Upjohn Estimate
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The labor force participation rate is a measure that represents the percentage of the working-age population (individuals aged 16 and older) who are either employed or actively seeking employment. Tracking the labor force participation rate provides insights on the working-age population and their engagement in the labor market.
Source: BLS LAUS, Upjohn Regional • (p) Preliminary, (e) Upjohn Estimate
Download Data


















NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





The unemployment rate is a measure that represents the percentage of individuals who are actively seeking employment but are currently without a job. The unemployment rate offers understanding into the availability of jobs and the overall state of the labor market within an economy.
Source: BLS LAUS, Upjohn Regional • (p) Preliminary, (e) Upjohn Estimate

NoteDescription, Source, and Data Download.





Tracking the average weekly wage gives insight to the income levels and purchasing power of workers within an economy.
Source: BLS QCEW, Upjohn Regional • Not adjusted for inflation • (p) Preliminary
